stem:
Ritu looks at an Amoeba under a microscope. It moves, feeds, and reproduces on its own. A classmate says it cannot be a complete living organism because it has only one cell. Bacteria are also single-celled microorganisms.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: The Amoeba is a complete living organism because its one cell carries out all functions needed for survival.
A cell taken from a multicellular organism is itself a complete organism.
All microorganisms are unicellular like this Amoeba.
A bacterium is an incomplete living organism because it has only one cell.

teacher.key_rationale: A unicellular Amoeba carries out all life functions in one cell, so it is a complete organism. A cell taken from a multicellular body is not itself a whole organism; not all microorganisms are unicellular; a bacterium is still a complete unicellular organism.
